title: Candlesticks
hook: Every candle is a decision. Green means buyers won. Red means sellers won.

launchpad.outcome: Read what a candle's shape actually represents, not just its color.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Does a long lower wick automatically mean the market is about to reverse upward?

steps.text: High and low: the highest and lowest points price reached.

slides.headline: Color comes from two prices.
slides.line: One simple relationship between them decides it.

check.prompt: A bullish candle closes ___ where it opened.

options.label: Below
options.feedback: Closing below the open is what makes a candle bearish, not bullish.

options.label: Exactly at
options.feedback: Closing exactly at the open would leave no real body at all.

options.label: Above
options.why: A bullish close settles higher than the open. That’s what makes it bullish.

slides.kicker: Two candles, two very different stories
slides.headline: Tap each candle. Read the shape.

tool.kicker: Two candles, two very different stories
tool.title: Tap each candle to see what its shape represents

candles.label: Large green body
candles.desc: A large body means price traveled far from open to close in one direction, a decisive win for buyers that period.

candles.label: Small red body, long wicks
candles.desc: A small body with long wicks means a real fight happened, but neither side settled far from where it started, indecision.

slides.headline: Long lower wick. Reversal coming?
slides.line: A trader assumes it means the market is about to reverse upward.

options.label: Yes, a long lower wick always means a reversal
options.feedback: No single wick is an automatic signal on its own.

options.label: Not on its own. Read it in context.
options.why: Right. A wick shows buyers rejected a push down during that candle, not proof of what happens next.

slides.quote: Candles are not just green and red.
slides.line: They show who pushed, who rejected, who held, and where price accepted.

slides.prompt: Isn’t a candle just green or red?
slides.modelAnswer: Color only tells you which side won that candle’s fight. The real story is in the shape, how big the body is, how long the wicks are, and where price actually opened and closed. A big green body means buyers won decisively; a small body with long wicks means neither side really settled the fight.

takeaways: A candle is a tiny record of a fight between buyers and sellers, not decoration.
Body size and wick length both carry information, read together.
No single candle is an automatic signal, context decides what it means.
remember: Every candle is a decision. Read the whole shape, not just the color.
